newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel wins Telia Internet access order.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel wins Telia Internet access order.

text.p: Alcatel Telecom said it had won an order from Swedish telecoms operator Telia to provide high capacity wide-band Internet access services using Asymmetrical Digital Subscribers Line (ADSL) technology.
A spokesman for the Alcatel Alsthom unit said the deal was the first such contract in Europe, following selection by Alcatel by the U.S. Joint Procurement Consortium.
"This first deal is for a 2,000 subscribers in Stockholm, but in the end Telia wants to cover 98 percent of Swedish households," an Alcatel spokesman said.
He declined to specify financial details.

A characteristic of ADsL is that it can use existing copper wire instead of new fibre optic, cutting installation costs. Alcatel said that ADSL could offer Internet access at speeds of 50 to 200 times the current 28.8 kilobit per second speed of analogue modems.

Alcatel added ADSL would also allow data traffic to use a telephone line at the same time as a telephone conversation -- solving a thorny issue in many Internet-linked households that the phone is out of order when the computer modem is being used.
